ai.description: The Thoda Bush Frog is a small, 20–22 mm shrub frog. It features a brownish-grey dorsum with dark mottling and a distinct, pale-edged dark interorbital bar. Its snout is acutely pointed.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes thodai* is best distinguished by the prominent, distinct white spots scattered across its dark-colored flanks, a feature absent in similar bush frog species.
ai.habitat: The Thoda Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Thoda Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes thodai* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in vegetation or tree hollows.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Thoda Bush Frog is endemic to the high-altitude shola-grassland mosaics of the Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu, India, typically occurring at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Thoda Bush Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" notes, typically heard calling from dense shrubbery or low vegetation within its montane forest habitat.
